paper_title: An Indium-Free Low Work Function Window Electrode for Organic Photovoltaics Which Improves with In-Situ Oxidation
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Advanced Materials - 2012 - Hutter - An Indium‐Free Low Work Function Window Electrode for Organic Photovoltaics Which/auto/Advanced Materials - 2012 - Hutter - An Indium‐Free Low Work Function Window Electrode for Organic Photovoltaics Which.md

knowledge_points.content: A bilayer electrode system consisting of a 7 nm Copper (Cu) film capped with a 0.8 nm Aluminum (Al) overlayer is used as a transparent window electrode in inverted organic photovoltaics.
knowledge_points.evidence: By capping the Cu electrode with an 0.8 nm Al overlayer this increase in RSH is prevented... Herein, we report an exceptionally robust Al:Cu alloy window electrode that simultaneously functions as the low φ electron-extracting electrode.

knowledge_points.content: The Al:Cu window electrode exhibits a sheet resistance (RSH) of approximately 18.5 Ω/sq (calculated from the 14 Ω/sq starting resistance of pure Cu plus the 4.5 Ω/sq increase upon Al addition) which decreases by ~15% (3 Ω/sq) upon oxidation.
knowledge_points.evidence: The RSH of 7 nm Cu film is ~14 Ω/sq... Notably, the Cu (7 nm): Al (0.8 nm) films have a 4.5 Ω/sq higher starting resistance than Cu only... the RSH of the binary Cu (7 nm): Al (0.8 nm) film decreases by ~15% [3 Ω/sq] upon oxidation.

knowledge_points.content: The improvement in conductivity of the Cu:Al electrode upon oxidation is attributed to the migration of Al atoms dissolved in the Cu film to the surface, where they form an oxide, effectively de-alloying the Cu and reducing bulk scattering.
knowledge_points.evidence: This increase in conductivity is attributed to migration of Al atoms dissolved in the Cu film to the film surface where they are oxidized. Since the RSH of the oxidized Cu (7 nm): Al (0.8 nm) film converges to a value 1.5 Ω/sq above that of unoxidised Cu films.

knowledge_points.content: The work function (φ) of the fresh Cu:Al electrode is approximately 3.11 eV, which increases and converges to 3.78 eV ± 0.02 eV upon oxidation in air.
knowledge_points.evidence: the φ of the Cu:Al electrode is very low to begin with (3.11 eV) and after an initial very rapid increase converges to 3.78 eV... φ of oxidized Cu (7 nm): Al (0.8 nm) films, 3.78 eV ± 0.02 (Figure 1).

knowledge_points.content: Inverted OPV devices using the Al:Cu window electrode achieved a Power Conversion Efficiency (PCE) of approximately 4.0%, compared to 4.7% for devices using standard Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) electrodes.
knowledge_points.evidence: the power conversion efficiency of OPVs using a 7 nm Cu electrode (~4.0%) is ~15% lower than that achieved using a conventional ITO electrode (~4.7%), due to the lower transparency of the former.

knowledge_points.content: The Al:Cu electrode maintains an exceptionally low root-mean-square (RMS) surface roughness of ≤ 0.6 nm over a 1 x 1 μm area, even after 32 hours of exposure to air and subsequent oxidation.
knowledge_points.evidence: the surface roughness of the films remain unchanged at an exceptionally low root-mean-square value of ≤ 0.6 nm (Figure 2)... rRMS at these two time intervals [3.5h and 32h] are given to show that φ and RSH evolve due to surface oxidation whilst rRMS remains essentially unchanged.

knowledge_points.content: The Al:Cu electrode acts as a built-in desiccant by scavenging oxygen and water molecules that permeate the photoactive layer, which is evidenced by the electrode's decreasing resistance when the device is stored in air.
knowledge_points.evidence: These electrodes also scavenge oxygen/water that permeates into the photoactive layer... This reduction in the resistance of the window electrode upon oxidation is used as a sensitive probe for electrode oxidation in-situ in OPV devices when the entire device is stored in air.

knowledge_points.content: Oxidation of the Al:Cu electrode surface improves the dark J/V characteristics of the OPV, resulting in an order of magnitude decrease in reverse dark current at -0.75 V.
knowledge_points.evidence: In fact, there is an order of magnitude decrease in the reverse dark current at −0.75 V which represents a large improvement in the dark J/V characteristic.

knowledge_points.content: To ensure uniform film growth of optically thin Cu, the glass substrates are derivatized with a mixed monolayer of 3-aminopropyltrimethoxysilane (APTMS) and mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane (MPTMS).
knowledge_points.evidence: Glass microscope slides... were exposed to the vapor of APTMS (3-aminopropyltrimethoxysilane) and MPTMS (mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane) at 5 mbar for 4 hours. The nanolayer derivatized electrodes were transferred to the evaporator for Cu and Al deposition.

knowledge_points.content: The efficient extraction of electrons is maintained after oxidation because the electrode's Fermi level pins to the LUMO of PC70BM (3.7 eV) via ground state charge transfer, as the work function remains below the PC70BM electron affinity.
knowledge_points.evidence: since the φ of the electrode remains less than or equal to the electron affinity of PC70BM (3.7 eV) it can be assumed that the degree of alignment between the electrode Fermi level and the LUMO of PC70BM remains unchanged, since ground state charge transfer from the electrode to PC70BM LUMO will occur pinning the LUMO near to the electrode Fermi level.

knowledge_points.content: Static secondary ion mass spectrometry (s-SIMS) confirms that the oxidized surface of the Cu:Al electrode consists of a dense, ultra-thin ternary oxide layer containing both copper oxide and aluminum oxide (AlxCuyOz).
knowledge_points.evidence: The surface sensitive technique of static secondary ion mass spectrometry reveals that for a Cu: Al (0.8 nm) film the upper most surface includes copper oxide as well as aluminium oxide... consistent with the formation of a dense ultra-thin AlxCuyOz surface layer.

knowledge_points.content: The room temperature diffusion of Al atoms within the Cu film is facilitated by the suppression of the Cu melting point in ultra-thin (10 nm) films, which occurs below 400 °C.
knowledge_points.evidence: This effect is attributed to the suppression of the Cu melting point due to the low film thickness, since 10 nm Cu films have been observed to melt below 400 °C. which in turn suppresses the temperature at which Al atoms can diffuse.
